newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine wants to expand T-bill market-c.banker.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine wants to expand T-bill market-c.banker.

text.p: Ukraine plans to widen the circle of participants in its Treasury bill market next year by allowing finance companies to buy and trade securities directly, the head of the central bank chairman said on Tuesday.

"We would like bring in specialised companies which believe in the potential of Ukraine's securities market and which could give commercial banks already buying T-bills some competition," Viktor Yushchenko told Reuters.
Under current rules buyers on the primary or secondary markets must purchase bills through a commercial bank.
Yushchenko did not say whether the finance companies could be foreign-owned.
"I would have nothing against it if we wrote up separate procedures for direct purchases by non-residential structures on this market," he said.
"I'm talking about serious financial companies, with a good image."
Although Ukraine's laws do not forbid foreigners to trade government securities, interest on their part in the T-bill market has been small because of unclear tax laws.
Yushchenko said the bank, together with the cabinet, has prepared a special document clearing up the tax rules and submitted it to Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko for approval.
The central bank plans to raise $852 million in T-bill sales in 1996 to cover the projected $2.6 billion deficit.

"Widening the market and enlarging the volumes on the secondary market would allow the central bank, as a participant on the market, to effectively regulate prices and influence inflation," Yushchenko said. --Natalya Zinets, Kiev Newsroom +380 44 229 2264
